articles.title: UFC 331: Tsarukyan se la juega y el peso mosca busca un cambio generacional
articles.standfirst: Esta noche se celebrará en Los Ángeles una de las carteleras más esperadas del año
articles.summary: Esta noche se celebrará en Los Ángeles una de las carteleras más esperadas del año
articles.body: Llegó el día. Esta noche Los Ángeles se vestirá de gala para celebrar el UFC 331, una cartelera numerada llena de nombres propios y de combates que darán mucho que hablar. La pelea estelar tendra un título en juego, el de peso mosca, y se lo disputarán Joshua Van (17-2) y Alexandre Pantoja (30-6) en una revancha muy esperada. Además, Arman Tsarukyan (23-3) vuelve al octágono casi un año después en el combate co estelar para medirse a Mauricio Ruffy (14-2) y acercarse al título de peso ligero. El duelo entre Pantoja y Van tiene todos los alicientes que necesita una pelea estelar para llamar la atención. En el primer combate, el brasileño se dislocó el codo en el primer asalto y perdió el título contra todo pronóstico. Por tanto, esta vez se verá de una vez por todas si lo del birmano fue un golpe de suerte o está preparado para dar un cambio generacional. Ambos han llevado su beef al siguiente nivel, son entretenidos de ver y tienen estilos totalmente diferentes, por lo que el espectáculo está asegurado. 24 años contra 36, la experiencia contra el hambre de ganar, el legado construido contra el legado por construir. El combate entre Tsarukyan y Ruffy tampoco se queda atrás, ya que podría definir al siguiente retador de peso ligero. Arman está obligado a ganar si no quiere dar aún más motivos a la UFC para olvidarse de él, ante un peleador que ha aceptado el combate en corto aviso y que no tiene nada que perder. Para el peleador armenio será un todo o nada, mientras que Ruffy sabe que el mero hecho de haber aceptado el reto ya le traerá beneficios en un futuro. De nuevo, otro choque de estilos. El striking estilístico de Mauricio contra el grappling de élite de Arman. Sin embargo, la cartelera no se queda aquí, ya que hay otros nombres que es importante remarcar para entender la magnitud del evento. Uno de ellos es el de Gable Stevenson (4-0), medallista de oro olímpico en lucha en Tokio 2021 y pupilo de Jon Jones, que se medirá a Sean Sharaf (4-2) con la intención de mantener su 100% de finalizaciones en el primer asalto y de paso acercarse de lleno al top 15 de la división. Tiene todos los ingredientes para ser una superestrella. Otro peleador destinado a llegar lejos en su carrera es Iwo Barianiewski (9-0), que tendrá en Alonzo Menifield (18-6-1) su primer gran reto para meterse de lleno en el top 15 de peso semipesado. Hasta el momento, el polaco suma tres combates en la UFC y tres K.O. en menos de minuto y medio. Hablando de K.O., el UFC 331 también supondrá el regreso a la compañía de Robelis Despaigne (6-2), medallista olímpico en Taekwondo, que se medira a Tai Tuivasa (15-10) en un duelo de acción asegurada. 'Bam Bam' está a una derrota de igualar a Tony Ferguson con la peor racha de la historia de la UFC, mientras que el cubano quiere demostrar su mejora en las MMA para asentarse en el peso pesado. En líneas generales, este evento lo tiene todo para hacer las delicias del respetable. Peleas mediáticas, enfrentamientos por el cinturón, y muchos nombres con un futuro prometedor que suponen una mezcla ideal para que esta madrugada todo el mundo esté atento. Además, una victoria de Tsarukyan podría acercarle a un futuro duelo contra Ilia Topuria, por lo que podría tener un impacto directo en el peleador hispanogeorgiano.

articles.title: Ayoub Ghadfa: "Lo que les molesta es que soy moro y estoy representando a España"
articles.standfirst: El boxeador, nacido en Marbella y que fue plata olímpica en París 2024, usa sus redes sociales para denunciar racismo tras dar su opinión sobre la situación en Ceuta en un podcast
articles.summary: El boxeador, nacido en Marbella y que fue plata olímpica en París 2024, usa sus redes sociales para denunciar racismo tras dar su opinión sobre la situación en Ceuta en un podcast
articles.body: Ayoub Ghadfa nació en Marbella. Sus padres, de origen marroquí, se habían trasladado a vivir a España en busca de un futuro mejor. Su progenitor es de Casablanca y su madre, de Fez. Por eso Ayoub se siente español y marroquí. El marbellí compite desde hace años por el país en el que nació y al que ha dado grandes alegrías. Campeón de Europa del superpesado (+92 Kg) en 2024, bronce mundial en 2023 y plata europea en 2022. Pero su mayor éxito para España, sin duda, ha sido la plata olímpica en París 2024. Pese a su exitoso currículum defendiendo los colores de España al máximo nivel, el boxeador malagueño ha denunciado comentarios racistas en sus redes sociales tras unas declaraciones sobre la crisis migratoria en Ceuta con Adel en un podcast. En él, Ghadfa dijo que opinaba "como marroquí, no como español". "Estoy avergonzado, nos avergüenzan de tal forma que eso parecía una jungla. No podía verlo. Yo estaba con mi padre, puse las noticias un día y dije ya. Porque ahora todos los moros somos invasores, somos delincuentes, todos somos unos violadores porque cuatro subnormales se dedican a hacer lo que hacen. No es justo que la gente piense así", dijo. Sus palabras obtuvieron por respuesta comentarios racistas. Él mostró algunos en su vídeo de Instagram en el que se pueden leer: "La nacionalidad te la da la sangre, nunca serás español", "Español de segunda", "Es marroquí, no regalemos la nacionalidad", "Eres moro, no español aunque hayas nacido aquí por desgracia". "Que le deporten"... Ghadfa ha reconocido en sus redes sociales que, aunque no suele responder a este tipo de comentarios, los hace porque está "bastante cansado" (...). "Y no pongo más comentarios porque creo que no merece la pena dedicarles tiempo", añade. En un post que titula 'A palabras necias, oídos sordos", el boxeador se dirige en un vídeo directamente a quienes opinan así. "No entiendo por qué la gente me critica o me juzga. ¿Qué criterio tiene para juzgarme o para decir si soy o no soy español? Realmente ellos, ¿qué han hecho por España? Probablemente no hayan hecho nada. Simplemente decir que son españoles. Sólo decir yo soy español y ya. Porque lo que realmente les jode, lo que realmente les molesta es que yo, que soy moro, estoy representando a España, me está yendo bien y les está representando a ellos también", dice. Y continúa: "La gente como vosotros, la gente así, no tiene ninguna aspiración en la vida. La gente como vosotros lo único que hace es sembrar el odio y yo creo que eso no es nada bueno, ya sea en España, ya sea en cualquier otro país. Y decirme que soy marroquí o que soy un moro, realmente a mí eso no me ofende, al revés, me enorgullece. Al igual que me siento orgulloso de ser español, porque España es mi casa y no necesito otro permiso para quererla ni para representarla. Así que como me enseñaron en el instituto, a palabras necias, oídos sordos", zanja.

articles.title: Isaac Okoh: Commonwealth Games gold medallist begins European Championship campaign | 'I can beat anyone in the world'
articles.summary: The European Boxing Championships are under way in Sofia, Bulgaria; Great Britain has a strong team in the competition with heavyweight Isaac Okoh looking to continue his winning run when he has his first bout in the event on Sunday; Okoh is the Commonwealth Games gold medallist
articles.body:
After underwhelming at the World Championships a year ago, Okoh has been on a fantastic winning run which culminated in a Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow.

He now wants to keep the momentum rolling into the European Championships, which are under way in Sofia.

Okoh has his first bout in Bulgaria on Sunday against Poland's Alexey Sevostyanov.

"I'm confident I can beat anyone in the world at the minute. It's going to take a really good fighter to beat me," Okoh told Sky Sports .

"There's a lot of great competitors at the weight. I feel like I'm up there and I'm in real contention for a gold medal.

"I'm well up for it and I fancy my chances against anyone at this tournament."

His victory in Glasgow has buoyed that confidence. "It's a dream come true, When you first start boxing the Commonwealth Games is one of the tournaments you dream of going to and then obviously to bring home the gold medal not too far away from home with friends and family there, it's a proud moment," Okoh said.

"It fills you with confidence going on into the future, Olympic qualifiers round the corner and the Olympics two years away.

"Since the World championships I've been boxing brilliantly. I knew I had to… I've been flying."

Britain has a strong team at these European championships.

"We've got a great squad. We had a brilliant medal tally coming back from the Commonwealths, one of the best in a long time. We've got a great squad at the minute, lots of talent, very young, fresh, hungry. So the mood's brilliant in camp and morale's through the roof," Okoh said.

"It's a great team and a great group of people to be around."

Although Sacha Hickey suffered a surprise loss to Croatia's Sara Beram, fellow Commonwealth Games medallist Ruby White got off to a strong start.

After losing in the flyweight final in Glasgow, White returned to action on Saturday and dominated Serbia's Nikolina Dzida, handing her counts in the first and second rounds en route to taking a clear unanimous decision.

articles.title: Caio Borralho: Arman Tsarukyan ‘going to get knocked out’ if he tries to strike with Mauricio Ruffy at UFC 331
articles.summary: Mauricio Ruffy has scored back-to-back knockouts going into UFC 331
articles.body:
Arman Tsarukyan and Mauricio Ruffy co-headline UFC 331 in a match that could determine the next in line for a shot at the lightweight title in 2027, and Ruffy's former teammate Caio Borralho sees the Brazilian with the edge on the feet.

Tsarukyan spent the last few months competing in wrestling and grappling matches outside the UFC while waiting for a date and opponent to re-enter the octagon, and Ruffy was selected as his next foe in Los Angeles on Saturday. Tsarukyan has won his past five in the UFC, capped off by victories over Charles Oliveira and Dan Hooker, while Ruffy floored Rafael Fiziev and Michael Chandler with violent knockouts in 2026.

"I think both guys are dangerous for themselves," Borralho told MMA Fighting. "I think Ruffy has the one-shot knockout power that he can turn off anyone in the division. I think if Arman wants to strike him, even if it's a little bit, he's going to get knocked out. But I think if he's trying he's trying to wrestle at least the first two or three rounds, I think it's going to be harder for Mauricio to keep the pace and strategy, the calm."

Borralho thinks it's "a 50-50 fight," breaking it down similar how his teammate Carlos Prates' potential welterweight title bout with Islam Makhachev might go.

"I think it's a dangerous matchup for both guys," Borralho said of Prates vs. Makhachev. "I don't think Makhachev ever fought a guy like Prates that hurts you, makes you feel pain and other stuff with the leg kicks and all the stuff. On the other way, [Makhachev] has the grappling. This is the antidote to the striking, right? I think it's a hard matchup for both guys.

"If Prates manages to keep his composure when he gets taken down, like he always keeps, his mentality is very good when he's on the bottom, and get up and defend a couple takedowns or at least make Makhachev a little bit more tired—I think Makhachev is actually getting used to the new weight class, so I think he's carrying more mass, more muscle, so this takes some time for him to adjust to that."

Makhachev recently defended his 170-pound title with a decision over Ian Machado Garry, improving to 2-0 at welterweight since vacating the UFC lightweight throne. Prates, who has only lost once in the UFC against Garry, scored knockouts in every other fight in the UFC and Contender Series.

"We saw [Makhachev] got tired in his last fight like he's not used to," Borralho said, "And I think if got tired like that against a guy like Carlos, he's gonna get hurt. But I think he has a massive chance to finish this fight too, to submit Carlos or anything like that, because he has a very good jiu-jitsu. But, in general, hard matchup for both guys."

articles.body:
Joshua Van and Alexandre Pantoja are finally going to settle their score.

The two flyweights first met in late 2025, in a fight that saw Van take the division's title after Pantoja suffered a fluke arm injury less than 30 seconds into the first round. Tonight, in the main event of UFC 331 in Los Angeles, they will finally run it back, with flyweight gold once again on the line.

The UFC 331 co-main event is also a huge fight, as Arman Tsarukyan takes on Mauricio Ruffy at lightweight. Both men are among the top contenders in the division, and could conceivably set themselves up for a title shot in victory. That's particularly true in the case of Tsarukyan, who arguably should have already had that opportunity.

Tonight's card features plenty of other exciting matchups. The main card will be highlighted by a fan-friendly bantamweight clash between Patricio "Pitbull" Freire and "The Korean Superboy" Doo Ho Choi. It will also include the latest appearances from unbeaten prospects Iwo Baraniewski and Gable Steveson, who will take on on Alonzo Menifield at light heavyweight and Sean Sharaf at heavyweight respectively. The undercard, finally, will feature an awesome bantamweight matchup between Charles Jourdain and Marlon Vera, a heavyweight scrap between Tai Tuivasa and Robelis Despaign, and appearances from fighters like Edmen Shahbazyan, Casey O'Neill, and Giga Chikadze.

articles.title: Drake Places Huge Bet on Joshua Van to Win UFC 331 Fight, 'I Don't Know Bro...But He Better Win'
articles.summary: Drake is heavily invested in UFC 331, particularly whether or not Joshua Van is able to retain the flyweight championship in the main event.
articles.body:
Drake is heavily invested in UFC 331, particularly whether or not Joshua Van is able to retain the flyweight championship in the main event.

The rap superstar posted a picture on his Instagram Story of his $650,000 bet on Van to defeat Alexandre Pantoja.

"I Don't Know Bro...But He Better Win," Drake wrote in the caption with the image.

The payout for Drake would be $1,098,000 if Van is able to win.

Drake is no stranger to placing large bets on sporting events. His biggest known wager to date is a $1.5 million bet on Argentina to beat Spain in the 2026 World Cup final.

That one didn't pan out with Spain defeating Argentina 1-0 in extra time.

Van, who is only 24, already has a 17-2 record in his professional MMA career. He has won seven consecutive bouts with three of the last four coming via stoppage.

Pantoja is getting a rematch with Van after their previous bout at UFC 323 ended in the first round due to an elbow dislocation when he was pushed to the ground. He had won eight straight matches prior to the accidental injury.

articles.title: John Hedges vs Pat Brown: Manchester-born Brown wins British and Commonwealth titles
articles.summary: Pat Brown continues his perfect start to life as a professional with a seventh successive stoppage to hand John Hedges his first defeat in front of a raucous Manchester crowd.
articles.body:
Pat Brown displayed destructive power to stop John Hedges in the sixth round and claim the British and Commonwealth cruiserweight titles in Manchester.

Brown started slowly in front of a home crowd at Co-op Live Arena but was rewarded when he got behind his jab.

A thudding left hook to the body dropped Hedges in round six and he landed the same shot moments later to wrap up victory.

An emotional Brown, 26, spoke of how "special" it was to win the British title in his hometown.

"I don't care about all of the belts, it's for my family and my people," Brown said on DAZN.

"I've had a childhood with them all but I had to go off-grid to train and they've always stayed behind me.

"And for Ross - my cousin, who I love dearly - I said to him I would go all the way and I will."

Brown extends his perfect professional record to seven victories, with each of those coming via knockout, while Hedges lost for the first time in his 13-fight pro career.

Dreams of Old Trafford - Brown targets British title and famous nights

This fight was originally set to take place in Altrincham, but Matchroom made the switch to East Manchester's Co-op Live because of ticket demands.

And the 5,000-strong crowd made themselves heard when Brown entered the ring first, followed by a chorus of boos for Essex fighter Hedges.

Chants of 'Oh Patrick the Bomber' and 'Sale' rang around the arena as Hedges took the upper hand in the opening rounds with his awkward style.

Brown looked for ways to set up his heavy power-punches, but Hedges' sharp footwork and holding at the right time nullified the threat.

The pendulum started to swing in Brown's favour in the fifth when he began using his jab to set up combinations, with a right uppercut punctuating the round.

Hedges paid tribute to Manchester icon Ricky Hatton at the weigh-in after the first anniversary of his death passed on 14 September.

And it was a Hatton-like rippling left hook to the body from Brown that sent Hedges crashing to his knees.

Hedges beat the count but was sent tumbling back down to the canvas with another blow to the midsection - this time he was unable to pull himself back to his feet.

Family man Brown, who made his ringwalk with his father, had previously said "putting belts on his dad's shoulders" was all that mattered.

After Moses Itauma and Conor Benn both experienced losses when skipping the British title route and heading straight for world title glory, Brown said he wants to go on the "journey".

Chris Billam-Smith and Lawrence Okolie are two examples of those who have recently held the British cruiserweight title and gone on to win world honours.

Brown now holds the British and Commonwealth titles, and could look to European title-holder Viddal Riley next.

Riley, 29, last fought in April when he secured a unanimous points decision win over former world title challenger Mateusz Masternak.

When speaking to BBC Sport on Wednesday, the view of Old Trafford - the home of his beloved Manchester United - sat in the background.

Not since 1993, when Chris Eubank and Nigel Benn's unification bout ended in a draw, has the stadium hosted a boxing match.

Brown said one day headlining at Old Trafford would mean more to him than belts.

Most importantly, Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn sees the vision: "Pat Brown, world championship, Old Trafford. I see it."

Brown still has a long way to go if he's to be mentioned in the same breath as former world champion Hatton, but he's used his latest opportunity to make his mark.

Featherweights light the fuse for UFC 331 at Crypto.com Arena inLos Angeles, where Chikadze (15-6, 8-4 UFC) awaits Brito (19-5-1,7-3 UFC) at 145 pounds. Frank Trigg administers the law and orderand gives the two combatants the green light. Front kick to thebody from Chikadze, who follows it with a straight left. Britoplows forward behind punches. Attention at UFC 331 shifts to the women's flyweight division, asO'Neill (11-2, 6-2 UFC) puts Moura (12-2, 3-2 UFC) to the test at125 pounds. Jason Herzog polices the proceedings. No glove touch.Moura comes out firing and knocks O'Neill off-balance. She catchesa kick and trips O'Neill to the floor, settling in half guard.Moura drops elbows and a few short punches. Crowd boos the lack ofaction, as Herzog hovers nearby. O'Neill reclaims full guard, buther Brazilian opponent postures and punches. Moura moves from halfguard to north south and lures O'Neill into an anaconda choke. Sheloses her grip after a few tense moments and returns toground-and-pound. O'Neill elevates the Brazilian, rotates her hips and transitions toa belly-down armbar in one fluid motion. Moura taps in what canonly be described as a stunning and spectacular turn of events .Clear "Submission of the Year" contender.

Next on the UFC 331 docket: a middleweight clash between Shahbazyan(16-6, 9-6 UFC) and Ferreira (15-4, 6-4 UFC) at 185 pounds. MikeBeltran provides the oversight. They start with a cordial glovetouch. Shahbazyan takes the center of the cage and scores with alow kick. Ferreira circles on the outside. More leg kicks fromShahbazyan. Ferreira not yet in gear with 90 seconds gone. Heswitches to southpaw, and Shahbazyan starts to attack the otherleg. Double jab from Shahbazyan. Beltran warns Ferreira forextending his fingers. Midway through the round. Shahbazyan stayson the low kicks and connects them to a one-two. Ninety seconds onthe clock. Shahbazyan stays patient, continues to throw leg kicksand evades the return fire. Surprisingly little output fromFerreira. Ferreira intercepts him with a left hook, resets andjabs. They trade at the end of the round. Sherdog Scores Brian Knapp scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan Tudor Leonte scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan Mike Sloan scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan

Back at it for Round 2. Shahbazyan again claims the center.Ferreira stomps at the lead leg and fires a side kick to the body.Shahbazyan drives home another kick to the lower leg. Ferreiraexplodes into a right hand but fails to follow up. Shahbazyananswers with a low kick, then gets back to his jab. They tradejabs, and Ferreira whiffs on a wild overhand right. Two minutes togo in the round. Nice one-two from Shahbazyan, then doubles up onhis jab. Ferreira misses with a spinning elbow but resets andconnects with a right hand. Hard leg kick from the Brazilianfollowed by a right hand over the top. Shahbazyan lands two bodykicks, then another. Ferreira stomps at the lead leg. Shahbazyananswers with a one-two. They exchange punches, and Ferreira catchesan eye poke. Stern warning from Beltran as the round concludes. Sherdog Scores Brian Knapp scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan Tudor Leonte scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan Mike Sloan scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan

Ferreira might need a finish with five minutes to go. He ups theaggression right out of the gate and steps into a right hand.Shahbazyan kicks at the leg. Ferreira knees the body and fires offpunches in combination, then jabs. Shahbazyan circles back to thecenter and returns to his low kicks. Ferreira answers with one ofhis own. Sharp one-two from Shahbazyan, who dodges a spinning elbowand counters with a low kick. Midway through the round. Hard bodykick from Shahbazyan, who resets and fires a left hook to theliver. Ferreira responds with a right hand over the top. Shahbazyanavoids a flying knee and clinches along the fence. The crowd booshis efforts. Ninety seconds on the clock. Shahbazyan scores withknees to the legs and drives into a takedown. Ferreira standswithout issue but cannot break free. Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is live TONIGHT (Sat., Sept. 19, 2026) with UFC 331 taking place at crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, Ca., streaming exclusively live on Paramount+ . The main event is a rematch for the UFC Flyweight title with Joshua Van vs. Alexandre Pantoja 2.

Joshua Van gets a chance to defend his UFC Flyweight title for the second time tonight when he meets former champion Alexandre Pantoja . Van was, of course, awarded the belt after Pantoja went down with an arm injury early in their first fight last year. Since then Van solidified his title as champion by beating Tatsuro Taira in one of the fights of the year. This is Pantoja's first fight back since suffering that arm injury.

The co-main event tonight is a five round non-title fight in the Lightweight division. Arman Tsarukyan vs. Mauricio Ruffy could fast-track someone to a title shot with Justin Gaethje. For Tsarukyan that would be his second title shot, if you count the one he lost on weigh-in day (due to a back injury) before he was supposed to fight Islam Makhachev. Ruffy has never been this close to a title shot, but a win here on the back of his White House demolition job on Michael Chandler would be a big statement.

The main card is rounded out by Patricio Pitbull vs. Doohoo Choi , Alonzo Menifield vs. Iwo Baraniewski and Gable Steveson vs. Sean Sharaf . This will be Pitbull's final fight on his current UFC deal. Iwo Baraniewski is worth keeping tabs on. He's won all his UFC fights so far in electrifying fashion. Steveson is, again, on course to be one of the biggest favorites in MMA betting history, that's in spite of him being just 4-0 as a pro.

The Featured 'Prelim' tonight is Marlon Vera vs. Charles Jourdain in the Bantamweight division. That portion of the card also has Robelis Despaigne vs. Tai Tuivasa , Michael Aswell vs. Joo Sang Yoo and Ryan Gandra vs. Ozzy Diaz .

The Early 'Prelims' kick us off with Giga Chikadze vs. Joanderson Brito . The early part of the show also includes Casey O'Neill vs. Eduarda Moura and Edmen Shahbazyan vs. Brunno Ferreira .

It's standard operating procedure tonight. Here's when the various portions of the latest numbered event goes live:

UFC 331 's Early "Prelims" will begin at 5:30 p.m. ET .

UFC 331 's Late "Prelims" are scheduled to start at 7 p.m. ET .

UFC 331 's PLE main card goes live at 9 p.m. ET .

All of UFC 331 airs on Paramount+ , which you can stream here .

The live blog will get underway at 5:30 p.m. ET, just before the first fight. Come in and chat with your fellow Maniacs in the comments.

These two patiently traded strikes in a pretty low intensity kickboxing match for the first two rounds (which Aswell was clearly winning). In the third, Yoo felt some urgency and started to land some big shots and then got a takedown. Yoo needed a finish then, but didn't do nearly enough to make one happen.

Ryan Gandra vs. Ozzy Diaz: Gandra took a minute or so to size up Diaz. After that he blitzed forwards and rocked Diaz with a combo. Gandra didn't wait around and admire his work, he kept throwing and put Diaz down along the fence for yet another quick TKO.

After the threat of the choke was over, O'Neill used the butterfly guard to push Moura into the air and then she caught Moura in an armbar on the way down. And then she made her tap!

Heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane has his next opponent lined up.

According to Nolan King of MMA Junkie, Gane will face Josh Hokit at UFC 334 on Nov. 14 at New York City's Madison Square Garden. That should put to rest any rumors regarding Jon Jones' potential return from retirement for a heavyweight title fight, at least for the time being.

In the women's division, Kayla Harrison will defend her bantamweight title against Amanda Nunes. That fight will serve as the co-main event.

Gane, 36, became the interim champion after defeating Alex Pereira at UFC Freedom 250. Tom Aspinall had relinquished the title due to ongoing issues with an eye injury. He is now 14-2-1 in his career.

UFC president Dana White previously said the organization decided against making him the undisputed champion, though it was announced Saturday night that he is indeed the undisputed champ.

Now he'll face the 28-year-old Hokit with the title on the line. Hokit is a perfect 10-0 in his MMA career and defeated Derrick Lewis at UFC Freedom 250.

articles.title: Gable Steveson KO'd by Sharaf in 12 Seconds, Latest Prize Money, Stats & Highlights from UFC 331
articles.summary: Gable Steveson's UFC career took a surprising turn on Saturday with a stunning first-round knockout loss to Sean Sharaf on the UFC 331 main card from the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.
articles.body:
Gable Steveson's UFC career took a surprising turn on Saturday with a stunning first-round knockout loss to Sean Sharaf on the UFC 331 main card from the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.

Steveson got a firsthand lesson in the unpredictability of MMA as Sharaf uncorked a massive left hook in the opening exchange that put Steveson out.

Sharaf left the crowd in disbelief. He was a longshot to even win, let along win by first-round knockout.

The underdog etched his name in history with one of the fastest finishes in UFC history.

Steveson's UFC record falls to 1-1 and his stock in the heavyweight division now takes a hit.

The 26-year-old is one of the most highly anticipated UFC prospects in recent memory with a collegiate wrestling career that includes a 103-3 record and two national championships. However, there are clearly some lessons that need to be learned before he can start competing for a championship.

Sharaf is relative unknown 33-year-old who had an 0-2 UFC record going into this bout. Taking a loss to him will put pressure on Steveson to re-establish himself as a prospect on a title trajectory.

The former Minnesota Golden Gopher doesn't want it to take five years for him to get to the top of the game.

"I think I'm closer than people probably realize," he said, per Donagh Corby of Bloody Elbow. "I'm still new, so I want my reps and I want to keep improving, but I'm not here to take five years to get there. I want that belt as fast as possible."

Clearly, he is need of more development, but the talent is still there for him to learn from this loss and come back stronger.

articles.title: UFC 331: Alonzo Menifield upsets Iwo Baraniewski despite gruesomely broken thumb, bone sticking out
articles.summary: There are some fights that just redefine what tenacity and grit are in mixed martial arts. This was exactly that.
articles.body:
There are some fights that just redefine what tenacity and grit are in mixed martial arts.

The first fight of UFC 331's main card Saturday night featured Alonzo Menifield taking on the undefeated Iwo Baraniewski in a light heavyweight bout.

Menifield came out of the fray victorious by split decision, but he was not unscathed. It was revealed that he suffered a total compound fracture of his left thumb …

WARNING: The following video is graphic.

Menifield, 38, persevered through the pain, fighting two more rounds despite the injury. The live-stream audience didn't even know there was an injury until a medical stoppage between the second and third rounds, when the referee noticed it and alerted the doctor.

After he was medically checked, Menifield continued to reassure the doctor he was fine to keep going, and he finished the fight, despite the audience and color commentators wincing every time he used his left hand.

The win moves Menifield to 19-6-1. He came into this fight off a first-round knockout victory over Zhang Mingyang. The light heavyweight competitor was ranked No. 14 for the UFC heading into Saturday and could be in line for a top-10 bout — once his thumb fully heals.

Baraniewski, the heavy favorite in this fight, suffered the first loss of his UFC career. He is now 9-1-0, and this was also the first fight of his professional career that went past the first round.

It marked the third fight that Baraniewski had this calendar year. Previously, he beat Austen Lane in March and Junior Tafa in June, both by first-round knockouts.

articles.title: What happened to Alonzo Menifield? 38-year-old boxing superstar overcomes all odds against Iwo Baraniewski despite scary thumb injury

articles.body: Alonzo Menifield was supposed to be the next name on Iwo Baraniewski's knockout list. The 38-year-old had other plans on Saturday night at UFC 331, and a hand injury that made an entire arena groan did not change them.The light heavyweight bout opened the main card at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. Baraniewski, an undefeated Polish fighter with a habit of finishing early, had never needed the judges before. Menifield, a veteran with a dozen UFC wins, changed that and collected the win.How Alonzo Menifield beat Iwo Baraniewski at UFC 331 with a broken thumbAlonzo Menifield and Iwo Baraniewski met on Saturday, September 19, and the first round belonged to the Polish fighter. Baraniewski, riding a run of first-round knockouts, stunned Menifield more than once with his right hook and put the 38-year-old on the mat. Menifield gave up his back but survived, then found his footing in a late scramble, according to LowKick MMA's round-by-round account.Round two followed a similar script. Menifield started fast and landed heavy shots. Baraniewski kept walking forward anyway and found the cleaner combinations.Before round three, the doctor took a look at Menifield's hand. MMA Junkie described a deep cut, and the fight went on. The veteran opened the final round by stunning Baraniewski, but both men were tired by then. They spent long stretches in the clinch until the referee split them up. After the restart, Baraniewski pushed the pace and landed the harder strikes until the bell.The scorecards told a tight story. Two judges gave it 29-28 to Menifield, and one went 28-29 the other way. It was Baraniewski's first career loss and his first trip to a decision, which left the Polish fighter at 9-1.Alonzo Menifield's thumb injury and the reaction inside the arenaThe full extent of the damage only came out after the decision was read. During the post-fight interview with Joe Rogan, Menifield held the thumb up to the camera. The Big Lead reported that a bone was sticking through, and MMA Junkie said the crowd let out a loud groan.The reports do not agree on when it happened. The Big Lead placed the injury in the first round, while MMA Junkie pointed to the doctor's check ahead of round three. LowKick MMA called it a broken thumb and said Menifield fought through it in the third.Fans did not need long to react. Barstool Sports posted, "Alonzo Menifield’s thumb is backwards and he’s still letting it fly" (@barstoolsports). Championship Rounds wrote, "ALONZO MENIFIELD'S THUMB HAS A BONE STICKING OUT" (@ChampRDS).The Big Lead reported that Menifield will not be back in action anytime soon, and none of the three reports give a recovery timeline. The 38-year-old is now 19-6-1 with 11 knockouts and has won two straight.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Joshua Van Beats Alexandre Pantoja, Judges' Scorecards, Prize Money, Stats & UFC 331 Highlights
articles.summary: Joshua Van removed any doubt that he's the top flyweight in the UFC with a unanimous decision win over Alexandre Pantoja to defend his 125-pound belt in the UFC 331 main event.
articles.body:
Joshua Van removed any doubt that he's the top flyweight in the UFC with a unanimous decision win over Alexandre Pantoja to defend his 125-pound belt in the UFC 331 main event.

The first fight between the two didn't last long, but the second one provided fans with fireworks early. Pantoja took the early lead with a successful takedown and grappling, but Van worked his way to the feet and both men landed impressive shots in the striking.

Some controversy started brewing in the second round. Van and Pantoja's heads collided, cutting Pantoja open. The Brazilian appealed to referee Herb Dean to no avail.

Pantoja didn't need the help from the ref. He found success with a takedown attempt and continued to put pressure on Van. As expected, Van was more than happy to respond with pressure of his own.

The two had several highlight-worthy exchanges.

The back-and-forth led to some tight scorecards heading into the fifth and final round.

The champion closed out the fight with his strongest round of the night. He scored a knockdown and nearly finished the bout, but Pantoja hung on to get to the decision.

The win vindicates Van as a champion since he took the belt from Pantoja in unique circumstances in their first fight. Van was declared the winner in under 30 seconds when Pantoja suffered an arm injury within the first 30 seconds of the fight.

The 24-year-old went to work and defended his title with a fifth-round TKO win over Tatsuro Taira at UFC 328 in May.

A four-month turnaround is a busy schedule for a champion, but he seemed to handle it well. It's a pace he seems to want to keep as he looks to stack title defenses.

"I always want to stay active," Van said, per Matthew Wells of MMAJunkie. . "If I'm gonna be training all the time, why not fight all the time, right? That's kind of my mindset."

Manel Kape could be the next contender in line. He hasn't fought Van yet, is on a four-fight win streak with four knockouts and he doesn't currently have a fight on the books.

If Van really wants to get back in the cage ASAP then Kape is the most likely contender.

articles.title: Van, Pantoja, Steveson's Next Best Fights After UFC 331 Results
articles.summary: Joshua Van successfully retained his flyweight title at UFC 331 with a unanimous decision win over Alexandre Pantoja.
articles.body:
Joshua Van successfully retained his flyweight title at UFC 331 with a unanimous decision win over Alexandre Pantoja.

Van used their highly anticipated rivalry to further establish himself as the true flyweight champion. After winning via injury in their first fight, it was important for him to get a more clean win this time around.

Now, both Van and Pantoja can move on from their rivalry and keep the division moving forward.

While Van was one of the card's biggest winners, the night did not go so well for Gable Steveson. The former NCAA wrestling champion was knocked out in a stunning upset on the main card.

Let's take a look at what could be on the horizon for Steveson and both main eventers.

There's really only one logical next contender for Joshua Van and it's Manel Kape.

There's already some heat between the two. They have gone back and forth about who is allegedly ducking who and a hypothetical title fight. With Pantoja now out of the picture, now is the time to make the fight happen.

Beef aside, Kape is the most logical contender anyway. He's in the middle of a four-fight win streak with four finishes, including knockout wins over Kyoji Horiguchi and Brandon Royval.

Working our way down the latest UFC flyweight rankings, Kape is the No. 2 contender behind Pantoja. Royval and Tatsuro Taira follow him up.

Van beat Taira in his first title defense and we just noted that Kape beat Royval.

At this point, Royval would be the top backup option to Kape, but this division needs to see Van vs. Kape before anything else.

Pantoja's run of success into his 30s in a division where youth and athleticism tends to reign supreme has been impressive. The reality is that he's now 36 years old and coming off back-to-back losses.

He needs a bounce-back performance and he doesn't really have the time to work his way back up the rankings.

A matchup against Brandon Royval would give him the opportunity to do that. Royval is a mainstay at the top of the rankings and Pantoja beat him in a title defense.

Royval is looking for a new opponent after his submission win over Lone'er Kavanagh so he could be interested in avenging a loss.

Tatsuro Taira and Kyoji Horiguchi would also follow similar matchmaking logic. Taira was last seen in a loss to Van so pairing up his two most recent victims would make sense to get one of them back in the title picture.

Horiguchi was on a nice run before a loss to Kape. It would be a good high profile fight for two veterans looking to stay relevant in the division.

It's still too early for the UFC to sell all of its Gable Steveson stock. His impressive wrestling background and athleticism are still a solid foundation to build on.

But it's also pretty obvious that his striking defense and chin could be barriers that keep him from reaching his potential.

The UFC is going to need to take a cautious approach to building him up as a contender. Getting knocked out by a relatively unknown fighter is the worst-case scenario. Now the matchmaking has to focus on a relatively inexperienced fighter who will allow Steveson to rebound without much knockout threat.

All three of these potential opponents have at least one UFC fight under their belt, but haven't been around long.

Freeman was notably finished by Josh Hokit in the first round. Terrance Chatman has some power, but was finished by first-round submission in his last fight while Guilherme Pat hasn't scored a knockout in two years with back-to-back decision losses.

articles.title: The Real Winners and Losers From UFC 331
articles.summary: To say UFC 331 was a wild night is an understatement.
articles.body:
To say UFC 331 was a wild night is an understatement.

We had a legitimately brilliant main event between Joshua Van and Alexandre Pantoja. We also had a potentially landscape-shifting upset, all-time submission, and an injury so gruesome that the thumbs up emoji needs to be banned.

Winner: The Van-Pantoja Fight We Deserved

We need to talk about Joshua Van's composure.

At 24, he has just defended the flyweight title against a legitimate legend of the sport. But it wasn't just the win; it was the way he won.

Van spent much of the first round on his back, slapping Alexandre Pantoja's ears, without making much effort to scramble away from danger. It was so nonchalant, and it set the tone to capitalize on a clearly emotional Pantoja, who perhaps had the first bout's freak finish in mind.

The Brazilian was visibly frustrated heading into the second round. He quickly became distracted when he thought Van illegally used his head, twice looking to referee Herb Dean when no fouls were committed. Pantoja's aggression set the pace, opened up opportunities for Van's beautiful boxing skills to shine, and led the challenger to become frustrated by his lack of damage output on the ground.

At no point did Van look stressed or in trouble. He is so methodical, so relaxed, that he forces his opponents to expend more energy than they should just to get things going.

That Van looked his best in the fifth round once again is an indicator that he's got the intelligence to back up an incredible skill set. He doesn't wilt in the face of danger - a demoralizing realisation that led Pantoja to coming up short once more.

The warning shot was right there for Mauricio Ruffy.

Not long before he was sent spiralling to the canvas, Arman Tsarukyan laid into him with a nasty elbow, thrown after a sustained period of pushing Ruffy up against the cage and trying to get him on the mat.

The first elbow landed. Shortly after, the next elbow came through a lot harder. Arman then held his struggling opponent up, before one more standing elbow ended the fight - and chatter over the No. 1 contender at lightweight - for good.

This looked all set to be the classic grappler versus the explosive striker showdown many expected. Ruffy even landed a shiner on Arman pretty quickly to play into that narrative, before getting away with a blatant cage grab to stop himself getting taken down.

Ruffy may have wished he allowed it to go to the mat. That grab directly played into the positioning and brutality of the standing elbow finish. It's funny how things work out.

That was a hell of a bad week for Gable Steveson.

It's fair to say the former Olympic gold medalist's fight against Sean Sharaf seemed to be cherry-picked for a simple win. Steveson is clearly a guy the UFC wants to push. He was the huge betting favorite and was expected to build on his debut knockout over Elisha Ellison before moving on to bigger things.

Sharaf turned out to be the worst possible opponent in every respect.

First, there was the press conference, in which Sharaf called out Steveson after he was arrested in 2019.

Then there was the fact that it took just one sweet left to shut off Steveson's lights in the third-fastest knockout in heavyweight history. He was out before he hit the deck — a crazy upset early in the career of a fighter many think will eventually see Steveson hold the belt.

That may well still happen, but Steveson's decision to leave the Octagon before the hand raise just reaffirmed that the last few days have been an unmitigated PR disaster for the Olympic gold medallist.

If you didn't catch the prelims, you missed Casey O'Neill likely earning herself $100,000 with one of the smoothest transitions into an armbar you'll ever see.

We're talking submission of the year potential after battling through Eduarda Moura doing everything she could to choke the Scottish fighter out.

It's the movement of it all. With 1:43 left on the clock, O'Neill is on her back. One second later, Moura's legs are pointing to the sky, as King flips the momentum and lands on her front. A couple of seconds after that, the 28-year-old stood upright and celebrated a career highlight that will be replayed all over the world.

Not since Mr Worldwide set a Guinness World Record for the largest gathering of people wearing bald caps has a Pitbull had such a big result.

"I'm sorry about the last three fights," commented Patricio Pitbull after his excellent first-round knockout of Doo Ho Choi. "I feel like that was my debut."

Finally, after two losses in his first three, the Bellator king has truly shown what he can do in the UFC.

Pitbull took complete control of an exciting battle with the Korean Superboy, who is always down to bang. His power came through against an opponent who is used to enduring plenty of pain, and he headed into Saturday on a three-fight winning streak.

The right that set up Pitbull's first knockout in the organization sent Choi into a slow-mo spin, leaving the door open for a simple finish and a burst of hope that the 39-year-old Brazilian still has enough in the tank to make a real go of his UFC career.

Hey, camera operator, was the close up on Alonzo Menifield's severely broken thumb absolutely necessary?

Atomic calmly asking Joe Rogan if he enjoyed his victory over Iwo Baraniewski while a chunk of his bone saluted the crowd - the top part of his appendage hat-tipping those in attendance - was a gnarly way to kick off a chaotic main card.

The juxtaposition of a man serenely enjoying his moment after overcoming a bruiser who wanted to take his ranking was kind of beautiful. His thumb, however, was not.

articles.body:
To say UFC 331 was a wild night is an understatement.

We had a legitimately brilliant main event between Joshua Van and Alexandre Pantoja. We also had a potentially landscape-shifting upset, all-time submission, and an injury so gruesome that the thumbs up emoji needs to be banned.

Winner: The Van-Pantoja Fight We Deserved

We need to talk about Joshua Van's composure.

At 24, he has just defended the flyweight title against a legitimate legend of the sport. But it wasn't just the win; it was the way he won.

Van spent much of the first round on his back, slapping Alexandre Pantoja's ears, without making much effort to scramble away from danger. It was so nonchalant, and it set the tone to capitalize on a clearly emotional Pantoja, who perhaps had the first bout's freak finish in mind.

The Brazilian was visibly frustrated heading into the second round. He quickly became distracted when he thought Van illegally used his head, twice looking to referee Herb Dean when no fouls were committed. Pantoja's aggression set the pace, opened up opportunities for Van's beautiful boxing skills to shine, and led the challenger to become frustrated by his lack of damage output on the ground.

At no point did Van look stressed or in trouble. He is so methodical, so relaxed, that he forces his opponents to expend more energy than they should just to get things going.

That Van looked his best in the fifth round once again is an indicator that he's got the intelligence to back up an incredible skill set. He doesn't wilt in the face of danger - a demoralizing realisation that led Pantoja to coming up short once more.

The warning shot was right there for Mauricio Ruffy.

Not long before he was sent spiralling to the canvas, Arman Tsarukyan laid into him with a nasty elbow, thrown after a sustained period of pushing Ruffy up against the cage and trying to get him on the mat.

The first elbow landed. Shortly after, the next elbow came through a lot harder. Arman then held his struggling opponent up, before one more standing elbow ended the fight - and chatter over the No. 1 contender at lightweight - for good.

This looked all set to be the classic grappler versus the explosive striker showdown many expected. Ruffy even landed a shiner on Arman pretty quickly to play into that narrative, before getting away with a blatant cage grab to stop himself getting taken down.

Ruffy may have wished he allowed it to go to the mat. That grab directly played into the positioning and brutality of the standing elbow finish. It's funny how things work out.

That was a hell of a bad week for Gable Steveson.

It's fair to say the former Olympic gold medalist's fight against Sean Sharaf seemed to be cherry-picked for a simple win. Steveson is clearly a guy the UFC wants to push. He was the huge betting favorite and was expected to build on his debut knockout over Elisha Ellison before moving on to bigger things.

Sharaf turned out to be the worst possible opponent in every respect.

That may well still happen, but Steveson's decision to leave the Octagon before the hand raise just reaffirmed that the last few days have been an unmitigated PR disaster for the Olympic gold medallist.

If you didn't catch the prelims, you missed Casey O'Neill likely earning herself $100,000 with one of the smoothest transitions into an armbar you'll ever see.

We're talking submission of the year potential after battling through Eduarda Moura doing everything she could to choke the Scottish fighter out.

A couple of seconds after that, the 28-year-old stood upright and celebrated a career highlight that will be replayed all over the world.

articles.summary: Joshua Van’s star continued to soar at UFC 331
articles.body:
Joshua Van showed he is truly one of MMA's great champions at UFC 331.

For nine months, Van had to listen to talk of his title fight win over Alexandre Pantoja being a fluke due to Pantoja suffering an arm injury less than 30 seconds into their first meeting; on Saturday, the flyweight champion answered all questions about his legitimacy as he outworked Pantoja for five rounds en route to a riveting decision win.

Pantoja, the once-dominant champion, gave Van everything he could handle, frustrating him with smothering wrestling and at times matching Van blow-for-blow on the feet. But the younger, more explosive fighter gradually pulled away as the bout progressed, stinging the resilient Pantoja with combo after combo until scoring a decisive knockdown in the fifth and final round to seal the deal.

articles.summary: MMA News: Sean Sharaf needed just 12 seconds to flip UFC 331 on its head. One left hook from the former Marine dropped Olympic gold medalist Gable Steveson at C.
articles.body: Sean Sharaf needed just 12 seconds to flip UFC 331 on its head. One left hook from the former Marine dropped Olympic gold medalist Gable Steveson at Crypto.com Arena, and the referee stopped the fight before the crowd had time to settle.Nobody expected this script. Steveson arrived as a heavy favorite with an unbeaten record, wrestling prowess, and Jon Jones in his corner. Sharaf had other plans, and the fallout hit social media within minutes. Fans were loud, blunt, and often very funny.Sean Sharaf defeats Gable Steveson at UFC 331 in just 12 secondsSean Sharaf beat Gable Steveson by first-round knockout on Saturday night in Los Angeles, and the whole thing took 12 seconds. The heavyweight bout sat on the UFC 331 main card, and few people saw a finish that quick coming.It came down to one exchange. Sharaf pushed forward from the opening bell and forced Steveson to give ground. Steveson dodged a right hand, but the miss left him open. Sharaf answered with a left hook that landed flush at the 10-second mark and dropped him. A few ground shots followed, and the referee stopped it at 12 seconds.Steveson entered as a -2400 favorite, backed by his Olympic gold medal in wrestling and a 4-0 record. Sharaf, a former United States Marine, was a +1500 underdog. He is now 5-2-0. Steveson drops to 4-1-0, and this is his first loss as an MMA fighter.Sharaf brought up Steveson's past at the pre-fight press conference, and the two went back and forth. The crowd booed Steveson loudly that day, which made it clear who fans were backing. He had Jones and coach Greg Jackson in his corner, yet neither could change what happened. Steveson did get up and talk with his corner and the officials who checked on him. He left the octagon before Bruce Buffer could read the official result.Sean Sharaf quotes Nate Diaz following his victory"The Smoke" broke down in tears inside the octagon once the result sank in. Then the mood flipped. During his octagon interview with Joe Rogan, Sharaf opened by borrowing Nate Diaz's famous line about not being surprised, expletive and all. Diaz first used it after handing Conor McGregor his first UFC defeat. The Crypto.com Arena crowd went wild.Sharaf then turned to the people who doubted him. "I believed in myself when nobody believed in me," he said. He also thanked the fans for their support and energy, and said he had worked hard and prayed hard for this night.The win also put his name in the record books. His 12-second finish is the third-quickest knockout in the heavyweight division. Between that result and the Diaz moment, Sharaf has gained plenty of new eyes. If the wins keep coming, his dream of ruling the division someday looks a little closer.UFC fans react to Sean Sharaf's win as Jon Jones looks speechlessJon Jones spent the night in Steveson's corner, and the cameras found him right after the finish. He looked stunned, then worried, as chaos filled the arena around him. Jones is both a friend and a coach to Steveson, and the two had predicted a heavyweight title fight for the Olympic gold medalist in the near future. This loss may have put that plan on hold, at least for now.Fans noticed the look on Jones's face too, and many did not hold back.Rob Kuhn (@RobKuhn_) posted: "this was suppose to be the future jon Jones?"World in Motion (@WorldInMotionHQ) went after the build-up: "Rogan spent weeks warning heavyweights about Steveson and it took Sharaf 12 seconds to make that warning look like a bad take"Ava Brown (@AvaBrownddbz) wrote: "Sharaf ending Stevenson's Olympic-to-cage hype in 12 seconds is the fastest anyone's changed my mind on a 'future champ' tag this year"Mr. Antiquated (@MrAntiquated) added: "Credit to anyone getting in the cage but I thought everyone said Gable was going to be some unstoppable force."LuckyRebel (@RBLOfficial_) kept it short: "I’ve had sips of water that lasted longer."Fans’ roasts were stronger as Steveson was the favorite to win for many.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body:
Joshua Van just delivered one of the best performances in recent UFC flyweight history. After getting his UFC flyweight title in less-than-glorious fashion in 2025 after Alexandre Pantoja injured his elbow within 26 seconds of the first fight, Van left no doubt on Saturday night.

In the UFC 331 main event, Van handled Pantoja's relentless grappling and picked him apart in the stand-up exchanges. Van was up on all three scorecards in the final round, but the champion defended his title in dominant fashion. Van didn't get the stoppage, but he did win all five rounds on card and four on the other two en route to a unanimous-decision victory.

Pantoja brought everything he had in his toolbox in an attempt to wrestle his title back from Van, but the champion was ready for everything that came his way. It was a great fight and an even better performance from Van.

The main event battle won the Fight of the Night bonus.

Arman Tsarukyan defeats Mauricio Ruffy via First-Round TKO

Here is a look at all of the results and bonus winners from UFC 331.

The heavyweight pulled off the biggest upset in UFC history when he shockingly knocked out Gable Steveson in the first round. It was the third-fastest KO in UFC heavyweight history. Take a look.

Sharaf earned the Proper Bonus and special additional bonus from Dana White bringing his total bonus money to $100,000. The other performance of the night bonus landed with Casey O'Neill. Take a look at the arm bar that earned O'Neill $100,000.

articles.title: 50-45?! Joshua Van blanks Alexandre Pantoja on UFC 331 judge’s scorecard
articles.summary: Alexandre Pantoja gave everything he had at UFC 331, but the judges were not impressed with his performance. Pantoja was looking to win back his flyweight ti...
articles.body:
Alexandre Pantoja gave everything he had at UFC 331, but the judges were not impressed with his performance.

Pantoja was looking to win back his flyweight title from Joshua Van after a fluke elbow dislocation cost him the belt back in December 2025. But after five hard fought rounds, the scorecards were solidly in Van's favor, giving the 24 year old champ his second successful title defense.

While "The Cannibal" pushed forward through the fight with reckless abandon and managed to land some of the best muay thai knees we've seen in a long time, it was Van's crisp striking that carried "The Fearless" to his win, and dropped Pantoja to two losses in a row.

It was clear by the end of the fight who deserved to win, and the judges picked Van by varying degrees. Ron McCarthy had Van winning all five rounds for a clean sweep, while Sal D'Amato had it 49-46 Van with Pantoja winning just the fourth round. Derek Cleary had it 48-47 for Van, with Pantoja taking rounds 1 and 4.

We'd say Cleary had the best card of the bunch. While not all shots are created equal, Pantoja landed almost twice as many significant strikes than Van in the first round. Round four was also a clear Pantoja round … to everyone but Ron McCarthy, anyway.

It's a shame to see the 36 year old Pantoja not getting his due on the scorecards, even if it wouldn't have flipped the decision to a win. The right guy won, but bad judging is bad judging, even if they got the outcome right.

articles.body:
The UFC handed out four bonuses after Saturday's card in Los Angeles, plus an additional promotional bonus that Dana White said he would match for the biggest upset winner in UFC history.

After UFC 331, four fighters picked up an extra $100,000 for their performances at Crypto.com Arena. Additionally, another got $100K in promotional bonus money and five fighters got $25,000 extra checks for finishes that weren't bonus-winners.

Fight of the Night: Joshua Van , Alexandre Pantoja ($100,000 each)

Joshua Van (18-2 MMA, 11-1 UFC) was dominant in a lot of ways against former dominant flyweight champion Alexandre Pantoja (30-7 MMA, 14-5 UFC) in their rematch, including a 50-45 score in his unanimous decision. The two slugged it out for 25 minutes and both left bloody, but Van, the second youngest champ in UFC history, now has two title defenses since he took the belt from Pantoja.

Performance of the Night: Arman Tsarukyan ($100,000)

Arman Tsarukyan (24-3 MMA, 11-2 UFC) had been tagged by Mauricio Ruffy (14-3 MMA, 5-2 UFC) and his left eye was swelling badly. His solution? Pin Ruffy against the cage, then unleash a sickening elbow that had him out cold with four seconds left in the opening round. The win almost certainly made Tsarukyan next in line for a lightweight title shot.

Performance of the Night: Casey O'Neill ($100,000)

Casey O'Neill (12-2 MMA, 7-2 UFC) was in some pretty significant trouble against Eduarda Moura (12-3 MMA, 3-3 UFC) trying to fend off a submission attempt. A few seconds later, with Moura on top, O'Neill got her feet onto her stomach and pushed her skyward like she was about to give her a childlike "airplane ride" on her feet. And at the same moment, she snatched her arm and in a blink had Moura tapping to one of the most insane armbars in history.

"Chaos" bonus: Sean Sharaf ($50,000+$50,000 match+$25,000 finish bonus)

Sean Sharaf (5-2 MMA, 1-2 UFC) was a ridiculously massive underdog against Gable Steveson (4-1 MMA, 1-1 UFC), who was a 24-1 betting favorite. But the former standout collegiate wrestler got absolutely embarrassed when Sharaf put his lights out in just 12 seconds, leaving him needing referee Frank Trigg to save him from further punishment. Even more absolutely pathetic, Steveson didn't even have the class to stay in the cage to hear Sharaf's name announced as the winner, earning at least some mild disgust from the broadcast team. For some reason, the UFC decided to forego giving him an official Performance bonus, though the decision-makers found a way to take care of him with the "Mobland"-promotion "Chaos" bonus for $50,000, which UFC CEO Dana White said he would match. It's worth noting that Sharaf spent the pre-fight buildup absolutely destroying Steveson for his history as an accused rapist. The state of Minnesota can thank Steveson, in part, for a change in state law. Steveson and a University of Minnesota teammate were arrested for suspicion of rape in 2019. But a legal loophole, at the time, said that if a sexual assault victim was drunk, and voluntarily drank, then they could not be considered "mentally incapacitated" and unable to consent. That, of course, is patently absurd, and the state of Minnesota fixed that law after cases like Steveson's.

Patricio Freire (38-9 MMA, 2-2 UFC) got his first finish in 2.5 years when he did something to Dooho Choi (17-5-1 MMA, 6-4-1 UFC) that hadn't happened to him in nearly seven years and put him out cold. The win was Freire's first stoppage in the UFC.

Marlon Vera (24-12-1 MMA, 16-11 UFC) had his back against the wall with four straight losses and five setbacks in his past six fights. But he pulled off the upset and took out Charles Jourdain (18-9-1 MMA, 9-8-1 UFC) in the third round.

Ryan Gandra (11-1 MMA, 3-0 UFC) knows nothing but first-round finishes in the UFC, and he kept that intact when he knocked out Ozzy Diaz (10-5 MMA, 1-3 UFC) in the opening frame.

Finish bonus: Joanderson Brito ($25,000)

Joanderson Brito (20-5-1 MMA, 8-3 UFC) ducked just under a slick head kick from Giga Chikadze (15-7 MMA, 8-5 UFC), and when it missed, Chikadze came off his feet and hit the canvas. Brito was on him in an instant, and moments later he had Chikadze out from his ground-and-pound in less than two minutes.

articles.body: Joshua Van may only be 24 years old, but there can be no more doubting that he's already one of the best fighters in the world.Nine months after their first meeting ended in one of the anticlimactic title changes in UFC history, Van and Alexandre Pantoja made good on their second chance, erupting for a thrilling Fight of the Year contender Saturday night at UFC 331. After five rounds of furious back-and-forth action, it was Van who ultimately emerged victorious, claiming a unanimous decision (49-46, 49-47, 50-45) to notch the second defense of his UFC flyweight belt and cement his position as the new-gen king of the 125-pound division."A lot of people said that was an accidental win the first time. Doubt me now," Van said post-fight."Shout out to Pantoja, nothing but respect from me. He's a tough motherf***er, man."Van (18-2) and Pantoja (30-7) first collided this past December at UFC 323, with Pantoja suffering a freak arm injury just 26 seconds into the fight to end his two-year reign as champ. The win made Van the second-youngest titleholder in UFC history, however most viewed the outcome as a fluke; Pantoja entered the rematch still ranked as Uncrowned's No. 2 pound-for-pound fighter in the world, while Van slotted well below at No. 10.The pair had essentially been at each other's throats ever since, with the animosity between them steadily growing throughout 2026 until it spilled over into an absurdly-paced, all-out war of attrition Saturday night at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.Pantoja off to a quick start!📺 @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/2caBtx4ZwB— UFC on Paramount+ (@UFConParamount) September 20, 2026 Pantoja, the decorated 36-year-old ex-champ, set the tone early, tackling Van to the floor with a slick takedown in the opening seconds of the bout. It was one of five takedowns Pantoja ultimately collected over the 25-minute contest, however Van showcased significant growth in his grappling defense since his title win over Tatsuro Taira in May, stopping 11 of Pantoja’s 16 total attempts and consistently refusing to be held down. Once on the feet, the champ was often dazzling, throwing punches in bunches and unloading a seemingly endless array of offensive combinations to the head and body.After allowing Pantoja several minutes control time in the opening round, Van shifted into high gear and seized momentum in the second and third frames, slicing open multiple cuts on Pantoja’s face and battering the Brazilian with his striking volume.An ABSOLUTE WAR through three rounds!📺 @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/koKGMpRagr— UFC on Paramount+ (@UFConParamount) September 20, 2026 Pantoja remained game though, and stole back control with his best round of the fight in the fourth. articles.body: NEW DELHI: At 12, an incident of eve-teasing changed the course of Suchika Tariyal’s life.What began as a need to protect herself eventually became a journey through judo, Ju-Jitsu and mixed martial arts. And on Sunday, the 36-year-old Rohtak native broke new ground for Indian MMA at the Asian Games.Tariyal defeated Mongolia’s Altanchimeg Baigalmaa 2-0 in the women’s traditional -60kg quarterfinal at the Aichi-Nagoya Games to enter the semifinals and guarantee India at least a bronze medal.In the process, she became the country’s first athlete to secure an Asian Games medal in MMA, which is making its debut at the Games.From self-defence to a life in combat sportsThe decision to take up judo after the eve-teasing incident was never meant to lead to a career on the international stage. But Tariyal steadily turned herself into one of India’s most versatile combat athletes.She began with judo before moving to Ju-Jitsu and eventually MMA in 2017. Her judo career brought eight national titles and international success, including gold at the 2019 Commonwealth Judo Championships and the 2019 South Asian Games. She also won silver at the 2018 Commonwealth Judo Championships and competed at multiple Asian championships.At the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, she competed in the women’s -57kg category and narrowly missed a medal.Her transition to Ju-Jitsu produced another major achievement when she won gold in the adults Ju-Jitsu Contact Female -63kg category at the 2024 JJIF Ju-Jitsu World Championships.Tariyal made her MMA debut with a victory in 2017 but took a seven-year break from the sport while continuing her judo and Ju-Jitsu career. She returned to professional MMA in December 2024 after signing with BRAVE Combat Federation and won at BRAVE CF 92 in Bahrain.“Judo set me up for MMA, which for me is the ultimate level of combat sports. Because of judo, I was skilful in ground fighting and grappling. I only had to learn the standing game and striking skills for MMA. Switching from judo was not difficult. MMA is a test of all-round skills, and one has to be a complete combat athlete,” she said.Second Asian Games, different storyThe Aichi-Nagoya Games represent a second chance for Tariyal. At Hangzhou in 2022, she competed in kurash, but the campaign did not produce the result she wanted.“Life has given me a second chance at the Asian Games. In Hangzhou, it did not go the way I wanted because kurash was not popular in India and my preparation was not adequate. This time, I am fully prepared for MMA,” Suchika told SAI Media.Supported by the sports ministry’s Target Asian Games Group (TAGG) scheme, she entered Aichi-Nagoya after winning back-to-back bronze medals at the Asian MMA Championships in January and May this year.Her rise has also made her a familiar face beyond the combat-sports arena. She has more than 300,000 Instagram followers and has featured on MTV Roadies and Prime Video’s India’s Ultimate Warrior. She has also been honoured by the President and Prime Minister for her international achievements and contribution to women’s empowerment.But for Tariyal, perhaps the biggest purpose of her journey is what it can mean to young women.“I really want to inspire young women to take up MMA. I will be very happy even if one girl looks at me and says, ‘If Suchika can, I can too.’ In modern times, women need to defend themselves, and parents must let their children take up combat sports. MMA gives you that complete package. And women have a strong mindset to play combat sports. They can bear pain and can be more focused. If a woman can bear the pain of childbirth, MMA is nothing,” she said.Now, with an Asian Games medal already assured, Tariyal is keeping her focus on the competition rather than the achievement.She admitted, “There will be no easy fights. I am not thinking of results now. I don’t want to put myself under the pressure of expectation. I just want to give my 100% for India. For any fighter, a medal is the ultimate achievement, and I am no different."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Van agranda su legado ante Pantoja y Taarukyan noquea a Ruffy en un UFC 331 histórico
articles.standfirst: El peleador birmano se consolidó como el campeón de peso mosca, mientras que el armenio se acerca al título de peso ligero
articles.summary: El peleador birmano se consolidó como el campeón de peso mosca, mientras que el armenio se acerca al título de peso ligero
articles.body: El UFC 331 celebrado esta madrugada en Los Ángeles ha tenido de todo, en una cartelera histórica cuyo broche de oro ha sido la victoria por decisión unánime de Joshua Van ante Alexandre Pantoja. Además, en el combate co estelar Arman Tsarukyan ha noqueado a Mauricio Ruffy en el primer asalto para acercarse al cinturón de peso ligero y a un posible combate contra Ilia Topuria en un futuro. En diciembre de 2025, Van se convirtió en el nuevo campeón de peso mosca tras aprovecharse de una grave lesión en el primer asalto de Pantoja, considerado el segundo mejor peleador de la historia de la categoría por detrás de Demetrious Johnson. Por tanto, en esta revancha habia mucho por decidir, ya que el peleador birmano no era considerado por algunos el legítimo monarca al haberse aprovechado de una situación desafortunada. Joshua dijo antes de la pelea que disiparía las dudas en esta ocasión, y eso hizo con una brillante actuación en la que contuvo los intentos de derribo de Pantoja en la mayoría de casos y acabó dándole una lección en el striking para llevarse la victoria y sellar la rivalidad de una vez por todas. Con apenas 24 años, no cabe duda de que está destinado a ser uno de los mejores peleadores de la historia de la promotora. Por otro lado, Tsarukyan hizo valer su papel de favorito ante Ruffy con un brutal K.O. al final del primer asalto gracias a un codazo que pilló por sorpresa al brasileño. Mauricio comenzó muy bien la pelea e incluso inflamó el ojo izquierdo del armenio, frenando por completo sus intentos de llevarle al suelo. Sin embargo, se centró tanto en el grappling que se olvidó del striking de Arman, que selló su sexta victoria consecutiva para acercarse al título. Cualquier otro peleador tendría asegurada con esta actuación una oportunidad titular, pero en el peso ligero hay cuentas pendientes entre Ilia Topuria y Justin Gaethje con una revancha que está más cerca que nunca. A nivel de talento hay pocos peleadores como Tsarukyan, y lo volvió a demostrar brillando con luz propia y dando un golpe de autoridad para pensar en cotas más altas. Ahora le falta tener más continuidad y reconciliarse con Dana White para obtener lo que lleva tanto tiempo buscando. Mas allá de estas dos peleas, hubo varias sorpresas que quedarán en el recuerdo de los fanáticos de las MMA. Una de ellas, y seguramente la más significativa, fue el K.O. de Sean Sharaf (5-2) a Gable Stevenson (4-1) a los 12 segundos. El pupilo de Jon Jones y medallista de oro olímpico en lucha estaba llamado a ser una superestrella de la UFC, pero en su segundo combate en la promotora su hype se ha caído por completo con un duro golpe para sus intereses. La cara del GOAT lo decía todo. Otro invicto que perdió fue Iwo Barianiewski (9-1), que en su primera prueba de fuego ante un rival rankeado en peso semipesado fue superado por Alonzo Menifield en una decisión dividida que pudo haber caído para cualquier lado. Una guerra en el striking que acabó con ambos exhaustos y pidiendo la hora. La gran decepción fue la pelea entre Robelis Despaigne y Tai Tuivasa, donde el cubano regresó a la UFC con una victoria por decisión dividida con sabor agridulce, que deja a 'Bam Bam' con la peor racha de derrotas en la historia de la promotora y a él en tierra de nadie en el peso pesado. Volvió a ganar Chito Vera, Patricio Pitbull noqueó y Casey O'Neill firmó una de las mejores sumisiones de la historia en un evento que será recordado por mucho tiempo. Grandes finalizaciones, grandes combates y la clara prueba de que las MMA son el deporte más impredecible del planeta. articles.title: Myanmar’s Van defeats Pantoja to retain flyweight title in UFC 331
articles.summary: Joshua Van earned a unanimous decision (49-46, 49-47, 50-45) win over his Brazilian opponent to cement his reign.
articles.body:
Joshua Van put on a striking masterclass to secure a unanimous-decision win over Alexandre Pantoja and retain his flyweight title in UFC 331 in Los Angeles, as the 24-year-old from Myanmar settled the score with the former champion after their first fight ended with a freak injury.

Undisputed flyweight champion Van cemented his reign atop the 125-pound (56.7kg) division, defeating the Brazilian via unanimous decision (49-46, 49-47, 50-45) in the main event on Saturday night.

Pantoja had suffered an accidental elbow dislocation 26 seconds into their first fight in December last year, resulting in Van becoming the UFC flyweight champion without an outright win over the Brazilian, who had reigned over the division for at least two years.

Van, the first UFC champion from Myanmar, defended the belt against Tatsuro Taira in May but was left waiting to seal his status as the best in the division as 36-year-old Pantoja recovered from the injury.

“A lot of people said that was an accidental win … well, doubt me now,” Joshua said after his second title defence, which extended his professional MMA record to 18 wins and two losses.

Pantoja took Van down in the first round before landing heavy punches and knees in a fiery exchange, as Van retaliated with a slicing elbow.

“You’re too good to brawl with this guy,” Van’s coaches told him during the break, suggesting a more tactical approach.

Van peppered Pantoja with left-handed jabs in the second round and rocked the Brazilian with a fluid combination of punches in the third. Pantoja controlled the fourth round as he took Van down but was unable to submit him.

In the final round, Van stalked Pantoja and knocked him down with an overhand right, securing the win on the judges’ scorecards.

In the co-main event, Armenian contender Arman Tsarukyan staked his claim for a shot at the lightweight title when he pinned Mauricio Ruffy to the cage, rocked him with a left elbow and knocked him out with a right elbow with four seconds to spare in the first round.

“I knew my time would come, so I was patient,” said Tsarukyan, who extended his win streak to six fights, as he called for a bout with champion Justin Gaethje.

In featherweight action, former four-time, two-division Bellator champion Patricio Pitbull (38-9 MMA) earned his first UFC stoppage win, dismantling South Korea’s Dooho Choi via total knockout (TKO) within three minutes and 28 seconds of the opening round.

Brazil’s Pitbull overwhelmed Choi with sharp volume striking before landing a devastating right hand that forced the referee to step in and stop the contest. Pitbull snapped a three-fight finishing streak for Choi, a promotional mainstay who has competed under the UFC banner since 2014.

In the heavyweight division, Sean Sharaf pulled off one of the year’s most stunning upsets, needing just 12 seconds to shock Gable Steveson with a first-round TKO.

Steveson entered the Octagon as a massive betting favourite, but Sharaf caught him immediately in the opening exchange, unleashing a blistering flurry of strikes that forced a lightning-fast stoppage. The 12-second finish marked the third-fastest knockout in UFC heavyweight history.

A visibly frustrated Steveson refused to remain inside the Octagon as Sharaf had his hand officially raised, while Sharaf celebrated the landmark victory in front of an electric crowd.

articles.body:
Joshua Van retained his flyweight title with a commanding win over Alexandre Pantoja in their rematch at UFC 331 in Los Angeles.

The 24-year-old from Myanmar beat Brazilian Pantoja in December 2025 after Pantoja suffered an accidental elbow dislocation 26 seconds into the fight.

Van, the first UFC champion born in the 2000s, defended the belt against Tatsuro Taira in May but can now claim to be the best in the division after soundly beating 36-year-old Pantoja again.

"A lot of people said that was an accidental win, well, doubt me now," Van said after extending his professional MMA record to 18 wins and two losses.

Pantoja took Van down in the first round, before landing heavy punches and knees in a fiery exchange, as Van retaliated with a slicing elbow.

Van, who moved to the United States when he was 12, then peppered Pantoja with left-handed jabs in the second round, and rocked the Brazilian with a fluid combination of punches in the third.

Pantoja controlled the fourth round as he took Van down but was unable to submit him.

In the final round, Van stalked Pantoja and knocked him down with an overhand right, securing the win in the judges' scorecards.

Scottish fighter Casey O'Neill also won on the night, beating Eduarda Moura with an armbar submission.
